comparator.name: Pharmacy (Farmacie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The Farmacie study path comprises a 135 EC required major and 45 EC of electives with the 7.5 EC bachelor thesis. The 15 EC thesis option instead yields a 142.5 EC major and 37.5 EC of electives. The example uses the first placement pattern in the official route table. The two patterns organise course enrolment and lead to the same curriculum. All three Academic Skills modules carry zero credits and are required. Passing the year-one module releases the credits for Onderzoek naar geneesmiddelen.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option supports drug action, disease mechanisms and experimental research. The quantitative option shares pharmacology and adds a distinct mathematical and computational sequence. General health psychology and ethics support some medicine-use questions without establishing a patient-facing pharmacy practice option.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address cellular and molecular mechanisms relevant to biological medicines; UCR does not reproduce pharmaceutical biotechnology or product development.
Both address endocrine physiology; UCR studies integrated human physiology rather than the complete pharmacy disease block.
Both involve experimental investigation; UCR supplies a broad life-science laboratory rather than medicine-specific pharmaceutical research.
UCR molecular pathology and genetics directly address neoplasia and cancer mechanisms, but not oncology pharmacotherapy as a complete block.
Both directly study infection and immune defence; the external course integrates these subjects with pharmacy.
Both address cardiovascular pathophysiology; UCR does not reproduce pharmaceutical treatment training.
The pharmacy skin-disease block remains visible; UCR has no dedicated dermatology or dermatological-pharmacy course.
Utrecht applies chronic inflammatory and autoimmune mechanisms to pharmacotherapy. UCR studies immune mechanisms in Infection & Immunity.
UCR Neurobiology and Pharmacology are each aligned once; there is no dedicated psychopharmacology course.
Utrecht introduces the pharmacy discipline and practice. UCR introduces cells, genetics and physiology in a separate biomedical course.
Utrecht studies neurological diseases and treatment. UCR Neurobiology provides nervous-system foundations and comparative approaches.
Both directly study drug targets, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity.
UCR Pharmacology addresses pharmacokinetics once; the external dedicated kinetics block remains separately visible.
The integrated pharmacy therapy block remains visible; UCR disease and pharmacology courses do not reproduce clinical pharmacotherapy.
UCR does not offer dedicated medicine-administration or dosage-form training.
UCR Biochemistry does not replace pharmaceutical chemistry.
Utrecht applies formulation, preparation, quality and analysis in product care.
The genuine 7.5-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.
The genuine 22.5-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.
Utrecht requires a bachelor thesis. UCR offers optional independent research in addition to the scheduled courses.
The genuine 15-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.

blocks.title: Medicine action, safety and health behaviour
Pharmaceutical chemistry, product care, practice and profiling

notes.text: The UCR options develop pharmacology, biomedical science and research skills. Utrecht also requires pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, product care and disease-specific pharmacy work.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Pharmacy bachelor studies how medicines are designed, prepared and used, how they act in the body and how their safety and effectiveness are assessed. This example follows the Farmacie study path.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The two UCR options connect pharmacology and disease mechanisms with either laboratory research or mathematical modelling and health data. Utrecht provides a more extensive sequence in pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, product care and pharmacotherapy.

curriculum.limitation: All three Academic Skills modules are required and carry no credit. Students complete the required first-year courses before taking required advanced courses.

cellNotes.text: Credits are awarded after students pass the first-year Academic Skills module.
Students take Neurologie before this course.
Students take Infectie en afweer before this course.
Students take Productzorg before this course.
This example uses the 7.5 EC thesis. The 15 EC alternative increases the major by 7.5 EC and reduces elective space by 7.5 EC.
In the standard 45 EC profile, at least 15 EC must be at level 2 or 3. Courses outside Utrecht University require prior approval.
